# PRD: Unified Pricing & Quote-Booking Consistency **Document Slug:** `price-quote-consistency` **Status:** Draft **Author:** Product Owner **Target Services:** `booking_system_backend`, `booking_system_inventory_hold_service`, `booking_system_frontend` --- ## 1. Problem Statement Galaxium Travels currently calculates and displays flight prices inconsistently across the customer booking journey: 1. **Explore vs. Quote Price Mismatch:** On the Explore page (`/flights`), the frontend displays seat class prices computed by the Python backend via [`_flight_to_out()`](booking_system_backend/services/flight.py:10) (e.g. Flight #1 Business = $2,500,000). When the user clicks "Get Quote", the Java Inventory Hold Service calculates a disconnected price via [`PricingService.calculatePrice()`](booking_system_inventory_hold_service/src/main/java/com/galaxium/holdservice/service/PricingService.java:19) using hardcoded base amounts and an arbitrary flight ID modulo multiplier ($2,500,000 × 1.1 = $2,750,000). 2. **Domain Model Desynchronization:** The Java hold service uses legacy seat class terminology (`"economy"`, `"business"`, `"first"`) and lacks support for `"galaxium"` class, causing Galaxium class quotes to fall back to the default economy base price ($500,000). 3. **Quoted Price Not Honored at Booking:** When a held quote is confirmed, [`HoldService.confirmHold()`](booking_system_inventory_hold_service/src/main/java/com/galaxium/holdservice/service/HoldService.java:104) calls Python's `/internal/bookings/from-hold` without passing the quoted price. Python re-derives `price_paid` using its own formula via [`booking.book_flight()`](booking_system_backend/services/booking.py:116), writing a price to the database that differs from what was quoted and held. This undermines customer trust, violates pricing predictability, and creates an unmaintainable split-brain pricing architecture across services. --- ## 2. Goals and Non-Goals ### Goals - **Single Source of Truth for Base Pricing:** Establish a canonical pricing authority so that catalog browse, quote generation, and booking confirmation always evaluate to the exact same price for any given flight and seat class. - **Seat Class Harmonization:** Align all services (Frontend, Python backend, Java hold service) to the canonical seat class domain: `economy`, `business`, `galaxium`. - **Guaranteed Quote Price Honoring:** Ensure the exact price quoted and accepted during a hold is persisted and honored when the booking is finalized in Python. - **Dynamic Pricing Extensibility:** Allow pricing rules (e.g., peak demand multipliers, promotional discounts) to be introduced in one designated service without causing cross-service discrepancies. ### Non-Goals - Real-time dynamic surge pricing engines based on real-time market feeds or complex machine learning models (out of scope for this refactor). - Multi-currency conversion or localized tax engines (prices remain in standard Galaxium Credits/USD). - Redesigning the quote/hold expiration lifecycle (15-minute hold window and background expiry scheduler remain as-is). --- ## 3. Current vs. Target Behaviour ### Current Architecture & Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber actor User participant FE as Frontend (React) participant PY as Python Backend (FastAPI) participant DB as SQLite DB participant JV as Java Hold Service User->>FE: View Flights (/flights) FE->>PY: GET /flights PY->>DB: Query base_price Note over PY: Multiplies base_price by [1.0, 2.5, 5.0] PY-->>FE: Flight {economy_price, business_price, galaxium_price} FE-->>User: Displays Flight #1 Business: $2,500,000 User->>FE: Click "Get Quote" (Business) FE->>PY: POST /quotes {flightId: 1, seatClass: "business"} PY->>JV: Proxy to POST /api/v1/quotes Note over JV: Hardcoded Map + (flightId % 3 * 0.1)
Base $2.5M × 1.1 = $2.75M JV-->>PY: Quote {pricePerSeat: 2750000, totalPrice: 2750000} PY-->>FE: Returns quote FE-->>User: Displays Quote: $2,750,000 (Mismatch!) User->>FE: Place Hold & Confirm FE->>PY: POST /holds/{id}/confirm PY->>JV: Proxy to POST /api/v1/holds/{id}/confirm Note over JV: Ommits price in payload! JV->>PY: POST /internal/bookings/from-hold {travelerId, flightId, seatClass} Note over PY: Re-calculates price: base_price × 2.5 = $2,500,000 PY->>DB: INSERT booking (price_paid = $2,500,000) PY-->>JV: Booking response JV-->>FE: Confirmed ``` ### Target Architecture & Flow The Python backend acts as the authoritative system of record for flight definitions and base prices. When the Java service generates a quote, it either fetches the canonical flight pricing from Python or delegates pricing validation, ensuring seamless consistency. The finalized quote price is then explicitly passed and locked upon booking. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber actor User participant FE as Frontend (React) participant PY as Python Backend (FastAPI) participant DB as SQLite DB participant JV as Java Hold Service User->>FE: View Flights (/flights) FE->>PY: GET /flights PY->>DB: Query flight & seat prices PY-->>FE: Flight {economy_price, business_price, galaxium_price} FE-->>User: Displays Flight #1 Business: $2,500,000 User->>FE: Click "Get Quote" (Business) FE->>PY: POST /quotes {flightId: 1, seatClass: "business"} PY->>JV: Proxy to POST /api/v1/quotes Note over JV: Queries Python GET /flights/{id} or uses shared formula JV->>PY: GET /flights/1 PY-->>JV: Flight #1 {base_price: 1000000, business_price: 2500000} Note over JV: Computes/validates canonical quote price: $2,500,000 JV-->>PY: Quote {pricePerSeat: 2500000, totalPrice: 2500000} PY-->>FE: Returns quote FE-->>User: Displays Quote: $2,500,000 (Match!) User->>FE: Place Hold & Confirm FE->>PY: POST /holds/{id}/confirm PY->>JV: Proxy to POST /api/v1/holds/{id}/confirm Note over JV: Includes locked quote price in booking request JV->>PY: POST /internal/bookings/from-hold {flightId: 1, seatClass: "business", pricePaid: 2500000, quoteId: "..."} Note over PY: Validates & records exact price_paid: $2,500,000 PY->>DB: INSERT booking (price_paid = 2,500,000, quote_id = "...") PY-->>JV: Booking response JV-->>FE: Confirmed ``` --- ## 4. Detailed Requirements & Specifications ### 4.1 Canonical Seat Class Taxonomy All services must standardize on three seat class identifiers: - `economy`: Multiplier 1.0× - `business`: Multiplier 2.5× - `galaxium`: Multiplier 5.0× *Deprecated:* `"first"` in Java [`PricingService`](booking_system_inventory_hold_service/src/main/java/com/galaxium/holdservice/service/PricingService.java:16) must be removed or aliased to `"galaxium"`. ### 4.2 Python Backend Service Updates 1. **Flight Detail API:** Ensure `GET /flights/{flight_id}` is exposed and returns the resolved seat class prices (`economy_price`, `business_price`, `galaxium_price`) as defined in [`FlightOut`](booking_system_backend/schemas.py:33). 2. **Internal Booking From Hold API:** Update [`create_booking_from_hold()`](booking_system_backend/server.py:242) and [`book_flight()`](booking_system_backend/services/booking.py:64) to: - Accept an optional `price_paid: int` and `quote_id: str` parameter. - If `price_paid` is supplied from an authorized hold, record that exact amount in [`Booking.price_paid`](booking_system_backend/models.py:39) rather than recomputing it. - Maintain backward compatibility for direct instant bookings by falling back to the standard multiplier calculation when `price_paid` is omitted. ### 4.3 Java Inventory Hold Service Updates 1. **Dynamic Price Resolution in [`PricingService`](booking_system_inventory_hold_service/src/main/java/com/galaxium/holdservice/service/PricingService.java:10):** - Replace static `BASE_PRICES` map and `flightId % 3` formula with dynamic retrieval of flight base pricing via [`PythonBackendClient`](booking_system_inventory_hold_service/src/main/java/com/galaxium/holdservice/client/PythonBackendClient.java:15). - Support `economy`, `business`, and `galaxium` seat classes. 2. **Forwarding Price on Hold Confirmation:** - Update [`HoldService.confirmHold()`](booking_system_inventory_hold_service/src/main/java/com/galaxium/holdservice/service/HoldService.java:104) to include `pricePaid: quote.getTotalPrice()` and `quoteId: quote.getQuoteId()` in the payload sent to `/internal/bookings/from-hold`. ### 4.4 React Frontend Updates 1. **Interface Contract Verification:** Ensure [`types/index.ts`](booking_system_frontend/src/types/index.ts:5) reflects consistent seat class naming (`economy` | `business` | `galaxium`). 2. **Visual Consistency:** Verify that the price displayed on [`FlightCard.tsx`](booking_system_frontend/src/components/flights/FlightCard.tsx:14) matches the total on [`BookingModal.tsx`](booking_system_frontend/src/components/bookings/BookingModal.tsx:314) and [`HoldCard.tsx`](booking_system_frontend/src/components/bookings/HoldCard.tsx:94). --- ## 5. Edge Cases & Failure Modes 1. **Backend Connectivity Failure During Quote Creation:** If Java fails to reach Python to fetch the flight's base price when creating a quote, it must return a clean `503 Service Unavailable` or structured proxy error rather than falling back to an inaccurate hardcoded price. 2. **Base Price Change While Hold is Active:** If an administrator updates a flight's base price while a customer holds an active quote, the locked price on the `Quote` entity must be honored upon confirmation up until quote expiry (`reservedUntil`). 3. **Quantity Multipliers:** For multi-seat bookings (`quantity > 1`), `totalPrice` must strictly equal `pricePerSeat * quantity`. Both must be consistent between quote and confirmed booking. 4. **Invalid / Unknown Seat Class:** Submitting an unrecognized seat class must return a descriptive `400 Bad Request` with `INVALID_SEAT_CLASS`. --- ## 6. Acceptance Criteria - [ ] **AC-1 (Price Parity):** For any flight in the catalog, the price shown on the Explore page for Economy, Business, and Galaxium classes exactly matches the `totalPrice` shown in the "Price Breakdown" modal upon quote generation. - [ ] **AC-2 (Galaxium Class Support):** Creating a quote for seat class `"galaxium"` calculates 5.0× the flight's base price and does not default to economy or fail. - [ ] **AC-3 (Booking Price Fidelity):** When confirming a hold, the `price_paid` recorded in the `bookings` database table matches the `total_price` recorded in the Java `quotes` table for that `quote_id`. - [ ] **AC-4 (No Flight-ID Modulo Jitter):** Quotes for flights with `flightId % 3 != 0` do not have arbitrary 10% or 20% markups applied unless driven by an explicit business rule shared across services. - [ ] **AC-5 (End-to-End Test Suite):** Existing E2E tests in [`e2e/test_holds.py`](e2e/test_holds.py:1) and [`e2e/test_smoke.py`](e2e/test_smoke.py:1) pass with zero pricing regressions. --- ## 7. Dependencies & Impact Analysis - **Service Dependencies:** - `booking_system_backend`: Changes to internal booking endpoint schema and flight fetching logic. - `booking_system_inventory_hold_service`: Dependency on Python backend client for flight pricing data; domain entity updates. - `booking_system_frontend`: API model validation and UI display verification. - **Database Migrations:** No destructive schema changes required. `quote_id` can be optionally added to `bookings` table as a nullable foreign reference. - **Breaking Changes:** No public REST breaking changes for frontend clients; internal contracts between Java and Python are extended with backward-compatible optional fields. --- ## 8. Open Questions 1. **Caching Strategy:** Should the Java hold service cache flight base prices locally (e.g. 60-second in-memory cache) to avoid an extra network round-trip on every quote request, or is direct real-time fetch preferred for consistency? 2. **Dynamic Pricing Ownership:** In future milestones, if surge pricing or route-based discounts are introduced, should that logic live exclusively in the Python backend or be isolated into a dedicated pricing microservice?
